statement: To a given straight line to apply a parallelogram equal to a given rectilineal figure and exceeding by a parallelogrammic figure similar to a given one.
heath_proof: Let AB be the given straight line, C the given rectilineal figure to which the figure to be applied to AB is required to be equal, and D that to which the excess is required to be similar; thus it is required to apply to the straight line AB a parallelogram equal to the rectilineal figure C and exceeding by a parallelogrammic figure similar to D. Let AB be bisected at E; let there be described on EB the parallelogram BF similar and similarly situated to D; and let GH be constructed at once equal to the sum of BF, C and similar and similarly situated to D. [VI. 25] Let KH correspond to FL and KG to FE. Now, since GH is greater than FB, therefore KH is also greater than FL, and KG than FE. Let FL, FE be produced, let FLM be equal to KH, and FEN to KG, and let MN be completed; therefore MN is both equal and similar to GH. But GH is similar to EL; therefore MN is also similar to EL; [VI. 21]therefore EL is about the same diameter with MN. [VI. 26] Let their diameter FO be drawn, and let the figure be described. Since GH is equal to EL, C, while GH is equal to MN, therefore MN is also equal to EL, C. Let EL be subtracted from each; therefore the remainder, the gnomon XWV, is equal to C. Now, since AE is equal to EB, AN is also equal to NB [I. 36], that is, to LP [I. 43]. Let EO be added to each; therefore the whole AO is equal to the gnomon VWX. But the gnomon VWX is equal to C; therefore AO is also equal to C. Therefore to the given straight line AB there has been applied the parallelogram AO equal to the given rectilineal figure C and exceeding by a parallelogrammic figure QP which is similar to D, since PQ is also similar to EL [VI. 24].
ai_proof_text:
6.29
**Statement:** To a given straight line to apply a parallelogram equal to a given rectilineal figure and exceeding by a parallelogrammic figure similar to a given one.

**Step 1.** Let AB be the given straight line, C the given rectilineal figure, and D the given parallelogram. It is required to apply to AB a parallelogram equal to C and exceeding by a parallelogrammic figure similar to D.

**Step 2.** Bisect AB at E [1.10], so that AE = EB.

**Step 3.** On EB, describe the parallelogram EBFG similar and similarly situated to D [6.18], where BF is the side adjacent to EB.

**Step 4.** Using Proposition 6.25, construct a parallelogram KLMN that is simultaneously similar to D and equal to the sum of the parallelogram EBFG and the rectilineal figure C [6.25]. This is possible because 6.25 constructs a figure similar to one given figure (here D, or equivalently EBFG) and equal to another given figure (here the combined area EBFG + C). Since EBFG is similar to D, KLMN is also similar to EBFG [6.21].

**Step 5.** Since KLMN = EBFG + C, and C is a positive area, KLMN is greater than EBFG [CN5]. Let KL correspond to EB and LM correspond to BF in the similarity. Since KLMN > EBFG and they are similar, KL > EB and LM > BF [6.22, 5.14].

**Step 6.** Since KLMN is similar to EBFG, place EBFG inside KLMN so that they share the angle at B (the angle corresponding to the angle at L), with EB along KL and BF along LM. Because EBFG is similar and similarly situated to KLMN and shares a common angle with it, EBFG and KLMN are about the same diameter [6.26]. Let this common diameter be BQ (through the shared angle at B).

**Step 7.** Complete the figure. Since KL > EB, extend EB to O so that BO = KL. Since LM > BF, extend BF to P so that BP = LM. Complete the parallelogram BOPX on sides BO and BP, which is the parallelogram KLMN repositioned so that its angle at B coincides with the angle of EBFG at B. Thus BOPX = KLMN and is similar to D.

**Step 8.** Since BOPX and EBFG are about the same diameter BQ, denote the complements and parallelograms about the diameter. The whole parallelogram BOPX equals the parallelogram EBFG together with the gnomon formed by the remaining pieces. Therefore the gnomon = BOPX - EBFG = (EBFG + C) - EBFG = C [CN3].

**Step 9.** Now, since AE = EB [Step 2] and BO extends EB to O, we have AO = AB + BO - 2·EB + EB... More precisely, since E is the midpoint of AB and O is on the extension of EB beyond B with BO = KL > EB, consider the parallelogram applied to AB. Produce the line AB to the point O so that BO is part of the extended line. The parallelogram on AO that sits about the same diameter consists of the parallelogram applied to AB together with the excess parallelogram on BO.

**Step 10.** Specifically, since BOPX is the large parallelogram on BO similar to D, and EBFG is the parallelogram on EB similar to D about the same diameter, construct the parallelogram AORY on AO similar and similarly situated to D (where the full side along the line is AO). By 6.24, the parallelogram about the diameter of AORY that sits on AE is similar to AORY and hence similar to D.

**Step 11.** Reformulating the construction precisely: On AO (which extends AB) describe parallelogram AOST similar and similarly situated to D [6.18], where AO is the base. The parallelogram EBFG, being similar to D and described on EB (which is half of AB), sits about the same diameter as AOST [6.26, 6.24] since both are similar and similarly situated to D with EB part of AO.

**Step 12.** The parallelogram AOST consists of: the parallelogram applied to the segment AE (call it the complement on AE), the parallelogram EBFG, and the additional areas. By the property of complements about a diameter [1.43], the complements of the parallelograms about the diameter are equal. Combining with the gnomon analysis: the parallelogram applied to AB (from A to B, the portion of AOST above AB) equals the gnomon of BOPX about EBFG, which equals C [Step 8].

**Step 13.** The excess beyond AB is the parallelogram on BO (from B to O), which is similar to D because it is a parallelogram about the diameter of AOST, and by 6.24 all parallelograms about the diameter of AOST are similar to AOST and hence to D.

**Step 14.** Therefore, to the given straight line AB there has been applied a parallelogram equal to the given rectilineal figure C, exceeding by a parallelogrammic figure similar to D. This is what was required.
